subject: Acme Health SOC 2 discovery \u0014 post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Health SOC 2 discovery  post-call recap and next steps

Hi Samir / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through Acme Health's security and compliance requirements. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key pain points you shared:
- Need SOC 2 Type II coverage and a clear timeline for evidence collection for the upcoming vendor review (internal deadline: 2027-06-15).
- Requirement for immutable audit logs and exportable logs for 7 years for select PHI-related flows.
- Data retention and deletion controls: tiered retention policy and ability to trigger deletions on request.
- DPA clauses around subprocessors and data residency; legal will want a short turnaround on a DPA draft.
- Pen test evidence and remediation history for the last 18 months.

What we can provide today (attached):
- redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf  high-level scope and controls mapping from our latest Type II report.
- pen_test_evidence_stub.zip  redacted penetration test artifacts and summary (stubbed examples; full package needs MPU request).
- dpa_draft_acme_health.docx  preliminary DPA draft with standard Redwood language and a couple of optional clauses for residency/subprocessors.

Answers / clarifications from call:
- Audit logs: we retain request/response and admin audit trails; logs are exportable in JSON/CSV and can be retained for 7+ years on request (we'll need to discuss retention storage class and associated cost).
- Pen tests: we run annual third-party assessments and maintain remediation trackers; attachments contain an anonymized sample of findings and remediation dates.
- Data residency: hosted in us regions by default; we offer Private deployments for strict residency or on-prem options.

Proposed next steps (action owners & timing):
1) Marissa: Share SOC2 summary + DPA draft (attached)  done.
2) Acme (Samir/Priya): Confirm which data classes need 7-year retention and whether any data must remain in a specific region  by 2027-04-29.
3) Rishi: Pull full pen-test package and remediation tracker; provide ETA for full package (expected 2027-05-06).
4) Scheduling: Technical deep-dive with your security engineering team to walk controls and logging export (30145 min)  propose 2027-05-03 or 2027-05-04.
5) Legal: Review DPA draft; we'll prepare a tracked-change version after initial feedback.

If that aligns, I'll book the technical deep-dive and route the pen-test request internally. Appreciate any corrections to the summary above.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0132

Attachment(s) referenced: redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf; pen_test_evidence_stub.zip; dpa_draft_acme_health.docx

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health SOC 2 discovery  post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa  very clear summary and appreciate the attachments. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Retention: We will need 7 years for audit logs related to PHI access events; other logs can be retained for 1 year. Can you confirm whether log export will include signer identity and IP addresses?
- Pen test evidence: we'll need the full report (redacted where necessary) and the remediation timeline for any high/critical items in the past 18 months. Fine if you need an MPU or formal request process, but want to lock the ETA.
- DPA: legal will want any subprocessors called out explicitly and a standard 30-day SLA for data access requests; we'll share feedback after internal review.

We're aligned with the proposed tech deep-dive  2027-05-03 10:30am PT works for our security engineering lead (I'll confirm with Priya).

Can Rishi own the pen-test package pull? Also curious on expected cost impact for retaining 7-year logs (rough ballpark).

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Director, Security Engineering
Acme Health
samir.khan@acmehealth.com | (650) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 17:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health SOC 2 discovery  post-call recap and next steps

Hi Samir 

Great, thanks for the quick follow-up. Addressing your bullets: 

- Log exports: yes  exports include timestamp, user identifier (SSO id/email), action, resource identifier, and IP in our standard audit schema. I'll attach a sample export template in the tech deep-dive deck.
- Pen test package: Rishi will pull the full report and remediation tracker. Rishi  can you confirm ETA (we discussed 2027-05-06 on the call; if longer please advise).
- Cost for 7-year retention: depends on volume; ballpark estimate for standard tiered archival would be ~1525% incremental on storage for audit logs at our observed workloads. We can run a quick sizing once Acme confirms data class volume.
- DPA: attached draft is the starting point; legal notes to you are welcome and we'll turn it into a tracked-change Doc.

I'll go ahead and tentatively book the technical deep-dive for 2027-05-03 10:30am PT and send a calendar invite once Samir confirms.

Thanks  looping Rishi to own pen-test evidence retrieval.


Marissa

Marissa / Samir 

I will pull the full pen-test report and remediation tracker. ETA: 2027-05-06 EOD for the complete redacted bundle. Deliverables will include:

- Remediation tracker (high/critical items with dates and status)
